title: Question 12
stem: Radon-222 ($^{222}_{86}\text{Rn}$) is a radioactive element found in atmospheric air. The decay constant of radon-222 is $2.1 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Show that the half-life $t_{1/2}$ is related to the decay constant $\lambda$ by the expression
$$\lambda t_{1/2} = 0.693.$$

markscheme_points.text: $A = A_0 \exp(-\lambda t)$ and at $t = t_{1/2}$, $A = \frac{1}{2}A_0$ so $\frac{1}{2} = \exp(-\lambda t_{1/2})$

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in radioactive decay law connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: $A = A_0 \exp(-\lambda t)$ and at $t = t_{1/2}$, $A = \frac{1}{2}A_0$ so $\frac{1}{2} = \exp(-\lambda t_{1/2})$; taking natural logarithms: $\ln 2 = \lambda t_{1/2} \implies 0.693 = \lambda t_{1/2}$

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem: Radon-222 is considered to be an unacceptable health hazard when the activity of radon-222 is greater than $200\text{ Bq}$ in $1.0\text{ m}^3$ of air.
parts.text: Calculate the minimum mass of radon-222 in $1.0\text{ m}^3$ of air above which the health hazard becomes unacceptable.

markscheme_points.text: mass of 1 atom = $222 \times 1.66 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$ (or molar mass $0.222 / 6.02 \times 10^{23}$)

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in radioactive decay law connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
Hint 4: Clearly show every intermediate algebraic substitution and ensure your final value has correct physical units.
parts.proper_answer: $A = \lambda N \implies N = 200 / (2.1 \times 10^{-6}) = 9.52 \times 10^7$; mass of 1 atom = $222 \times 1.66 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg}$ (or molar mass $0.222 / 6.02 \times 10^{23}$); mass = $(9.52 \times 10^7 \times 0.222) / (6.02 \times 10^{23})$; mass = $3.5 \times 10^{-17}\text{ kg}$
